SECTION 5.01. Financial Statements and
Other Information . The Borrowers will furnish to the Administrative Agent and each Lender:

(a) within ninety (90) days after the
end of each fiscal year of the Company (or, if earlier, by the date that the Annual Report on Form 10-K of the Company for such fiscal year would be required to be filed under the rules and regulations of the
SEC, giving effect to any automatic extension available thereunder for the filing of such form) (commencing with the fiscal year ending December 31, 2022), its audited consolidated balance sheet and related statements of operations,
stockholders’ equity and cash flows as of the end of and for such year, setting forth in each case in comparative form the figures for the previous fiscal year, all reported on by independent public accountants of recognized national standing
(without a “going concern” or like qualification, commentary or exception, and without any qualification or exception as to the scope of such audit) to the effect that such consolidated financial statements present fairly in all material
respects the financial condition and results of operations of the Company and its consolidated Subsidiaries on a consolidated basis in accordance with GAAP consistently applied;

(b) within forty-five (45) days after the end of each of the first three fiscal quarters of each fiscal year of the Company (or, if
earlier, by the date that the Quarterly Report on Form 10 Q of the Company for such fiscal quarter would be required to be filed under the rules and regulations of the SEC, giving effect to any automatic extension available thereunder for the filing
of such form) (commencing with

findings.sourceCitation: §5.01(c)(iv) - this is where the operative source text provided to me for verification ends, mid-sentence, on an open parenthesis
findings.proposedIrEvidence: Rule ir-rule:1efa76ec29a69b5b04670269 (5.01(d)) excerpt: 'as soon as available, but in any event no later than forty-five (45) days following the end of each fiscal year of the Company, a copy of the plan ... (the "Projections") in form reasonably satisfactory to the Administrative Agent'; Rule ir-rule:3469133ef9c241eb2c0f839a (5.01(e)) excerpt about SEC/exchange filings; Rule ir-rule:bb1b6389d2b37da6c4e51da8 (5.01(f)) excerpt about SEC correspondence; all marked sufficiency: COMPLETE, plus a 'Projections' definition marked sufficiency: COMPLETE.
findings.verifierReasoning: The operative source text I was given for Section 5.01 stops abruptly mid-sentence within clause (c)(iv) ('...as of the date of delivery of such certificate ('). No text corresponding to clauses (d), (e), or (f), and no text defining 'Projections,' was included anywhere in the source material or retrieved context provided to me. Yet the proposed IR confidently asserts three additional rules (5.01(d), (e), (f)) and a 'Projections' definition, each with detailed quoted excerpts and each marked sufficiency COMPLETE. I have no way to independently confirm that these excerpts are accurate quotations of the real contract, that they appear in the section the IR cites, or that no further provisos/exceptions attach to them (the same way a genuine proviso was dropped in the worked example). Because sufficiency is asserted as COMPLETE for content I cannot corroborate at all, this is exactly the kind of confident-but-unverifiable claim that deserves heightened scrutiny. I cannot resolve from the evidence given whether this is a faithful representation of real contract text I simply wasn't shown, or an unsupported/fabricated addition - hence UNCERTAIN rather than a hard MATERIAL or NON_MATERIAL call.

findings.proposedIrEvidence: dependsOn: [{relationshipType: REQUIRES, targetRuleId: ir-rule:1689ab0ecacf9c3d28b7ab99 (clause (a)), description: 'Compliance Certificate is delivered concurrently with annual financial statements under clause (a).'}, {relationshipType: REQUIRES, targetRuleId: ir-rule:af5a73aff939dde2ec0d2a66 (clause (b)), description: 'Compliance Certificate is delivered concurrently with quarterly financial statements under clause (b).'}]
findings.verifierReasoning: The source text uses a disjunctive trigger - the Compliance Certificate must accompany 'any delivery of financial statements under clause (a) or (b)' - meaning each delivery event under either (a) or (b) independently triggers a corresponding certificate delivery (an annual CC concurrent with annual statements, and a separate quarterly CC concurrent with quarterly statements). The proposed IR represents this as two separate REQUIRES dependency edges to both the (a)-rule and the (b)-rule. If a downstream consumer of this IR treats multiple REQUIRES entries under dependsOn as a conjunctive precondition (i.e., that a Compliance Certificate delivery requires both an (a) delivery AND a (b) delivery to have occurred), that would misrepresent the source, which requires a certificate concurrently with each type of delivery independently, not only when both occur together. I cannot tell from the IR schema alone how a downstream engine will resolve multiple dependsOn entries, so I cannot confirm this is actually being misread as AND, but the structure is genuinely ambiguous relative to the source's clearly disjunctive ('or') phrasing.

findings.proposedIrEvidence: entityScope: [] and entityScopeExcluded: [] for every one of the 6 compiled rules (ir-rule:1689ab0ecacf9c3d28b7ab99, af5a73aff939dde2ec0d2a66, 36d0e82c520ef8dd00208fec, 1efa76ec29a69b5b04670269, 3469133ef9c241eb2c0f839a, bb1b6389d2b37da6c4e51da8)
findings.verifierReasoning: The deterministic pass flagged that the source distinguishes multiple entity-scope terms (Restricted/Unrestricted Subsidiary) while the IR records no entity-scope restriction anywhere. Investigating this: the Restricted/Unrestricted Subsidiary language in (c)(iv) describes content the Compliance Certificate must list (a categorization requirement), not a restriction on who owes the underlying reporting obligation, and it is already captured as a condition (rule[r_c].condition[4]), so that specific signal does not appear to reflect a missing rule. However, independently of that signal, I note the operative preamble explicitly identifies 'The Borrowers' as the obligated party for the entire Section 5.01 furnishing obligation, and this obligor identification is not captured in entityScope for any of the 6 rules - it is empty across the board. Whether this is a real semantic gap depends on how entityScope is meant to be populated/used for affirmative (obligation) covenants versus negative (basket/restriction) covenants elsewhere in this IR schema, which I cannot fully determine from the material given. I flag this as an open, unresolved point rather than a confirmed defect.
